quoteAdmin.display.title: Display request efficiency
quoteAdmin.display.scope: Counters cover browser display requests in this process and survive cache clearing. Restart resets them. Live and historical routes are separate; a fallback may make one request to each. Batch symbol counts deduplicate within each request. Logical loads can make zero or several HTTP calls; actual vendor traffic is below. Percentiles use bounded latency buckets, include failures and shared-load waits, and report an upper bound. Source latency below runs from dispatch through body close.

Calls are logical source reads (including adjustment checks), not HTTP totals; HTTP counts cover shadow traffic only. Refusals are separate from source failures. forecast.methodology.population: The earliest accepted set for each stock in a cohort decides membership. A degraded or mismatched first set excludes that stock; reruns cannot replace it. Pre-live, test and off-benchmark sets are excluded and counted separately.
forecast.methodology.gates: Metrics are published only for closed cohorts with terminal checkpoints, at least 30 eligible observations and no more than 5% final refusals. Corporate actions are excluded and counted; halted stocks remain included at their last traded close.
forecast.methodology.statistics: Excess returns use each set's frozen benchmark. Label permutations retain realised excess returns while shuffling predictions; Benjamini–Hochberg correction is applied within each cell. Custom ranges are exploratory: p* does not correct for choosing the range.
forecast.methodology.sources: Scored closes come from Tencent's unadjusted daily bars. Adjusted prices are used only to detect corporate actions and are never scored. A source failure defers settlement; it does not become a final refusal.

sso.guide.saml.step1.google: Google Admin → Apps → Web and mobile apps → Add app → Add custom SAML app.
sso.guide.saml.step1.keycloak: Keycloak → your realm → Clients → Create client → client type SAML.
sso.guide.saml.step1.okta: Okta Admin → Applications → Create App Integration → SAML 2.0.
sso.guide.saml.step2: Give the identity provider the portal's two addresses
sso.guide.saml.step2.body: These identify this portal and tell the identity provider where to send the signed assertion. They are derived from the site's public URL and must match exactly.
sso.guide.saml.step3: Check which attributes the assertion carries
sso.guide.saml.step3.body: The portal needs a stable user identifier, and can use an email, a display name and group names if they are sent. Entra sends its defaults (user.userprincipalname, user.mail, user.displayname) with no extra work; groups have to be added as a claim. Whatever names your identity provider uses, enter them in the attribute mapping below.
sso.guide.saml.step4: Bring the identity provider's metadata back here
sso.guide.saml.step4.body: Paste its metadata URL into the field below and use "Fetch metadata" — that is what supplies the signing certificate. Find it at:
sso.guide.step5.body: Sign out, then use the single sign-on button on the login page. If provisioning is off, the account must already exist in the portal and be linked — otherwise the sign-in is refused rather than creating a stranger an account.
